Cyber Attack Disrupts Construction Materials Firms Across DRC

A widespread cyber attack targeting the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s Construction Materials industry has disrupted operations at several companies, with ransomware crippling critical IT systems and halting production at a number of manufacturing sites. The incident, which began in the early hours of Tuesday, is ongoing and has led to significant operational setbacks for firms supplying cement, bricks, aggregates, and related products throughout the country.

Sources within the industry say the attack has encrypted essential data on the networks of at least five major producers, including KinCem Materials, CongoBuild Solutions, and Lubumbashi Aggregates. Production lines at affected plants have been idled as employees are unable to access digital control systems or inventory records. Several plants in and around Kinshasa and Lubumbashi remain offline, with management teams working to assess the full extent of the breach.

“We have shut down all automated systems as a precaution,” said Alain Mwamba, Chief Operating Officer at KinCem Materials. “Our IT teams are working around the clock with external cybersecurity specialists, but at this stage, we cannot estimate when normal operations will resume.”

The Construction Materials Trade Union confirmed that hundreds of workers across multiple sites have been instructed to remain at home while systems are restored and security protocols are reviewed. “We are concerned for the immediate welfare of our members,” said union spokesperson Marie-Bernadette Mputu. “Many rely on daily wages, and the uncertainty is causing hardship.”

Industry analysts warn that the ongoing disruption may delay construction schedules and put pressure on local supply chains. “This attack has exposed a critical vulnerability in the sector’s digital infrastructure,” observed Jean-Pierre Kazadi, an independent industry consultant based in Kinshasa. “Firms will need to invest more heavily in cybersecurity to prevent future incidents.”

The Construction Materials Association of Congo has called for industry-wide cooperation and information sharing as the situation develops. “This is an unprecedented challenge for our sector,” said association president Clément Nlandu. “We urge all members to be vigilant and to support each other during this difficult time.”

The full impact of the attack remains unclear as investigations continue.
